A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the AI-Face dataset and fairness benchmark. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial changes to annotations and experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original annotator evaluations, human annotation-quality assessments, detector benchmarks, robustness experiments, and generalization analyses.

after.justification: V3 reports original annotation assessments and detector experiments, including additional training-ratio, age-subgroup, and CLIP+MLP results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: V1's joint gender/age/race annotator with cross-entropy, dropout uncertainty, and human correction is substantially redesigned. V3 uses separate gender and age annotators with vector-scaling and Sinkhorn fairness losses, plus landmark masking, K-means, and color matching for skin tone. Uncertainty-guided correction disappears; human labeling remains for evaluation. Appendix D.7 also introduces a CLIP+MLP detector.

E1.justification: V3 replaces race classification with ten skin-tone categories and changes four age categories to five defined age bands. It removes CASIA-WebFace and CelebA as real-image sources, replaces VGGFace2 with IMDB-WIKI for annotator training, and drops Adience evaluation. CCv2, containing real faces with self-reported demographics, replaces A-DF-1.0 in generalization testing. The 37 fake-generation methods remain.

E2.justification: The main twelve detectors and the Face++/InsightFace annotator comparators remain. V3 adds a limited comparison involving the new CLIP+MLP detector against EfficientB4, SPSL, UnivFD, and PG-FDD in Table D.9.

E3.justification: Reported detector training increases from five to ten epochs. Intersectional evaluation changes from eight gender-by-race groups to six gender-by-tone groups. V3 removes average fairness ranks, adds overall FPR reporting, and revises individual fairness, including delta from 0.06 to 0.08. Distortion defaults also change: JPEG quality 60 to 80, brightness/contrast limit 0.2 to 0.4, and rotation from ±45 to ±30 degrees. Annotation-audit sampling is redesigned.

E4.justification: V3 adds frequency-spectrum analysis, age-subgroup error analysis, controlled real-to-fake ratio experiments, and the foundation-model investigation. It removes v1's uncertainty-stratified annotator analysis, human-correction ablations, FF++-trained transfer experiment, and fairness–utility trade-off study. Training-size and distortion-sensitivity analyses remain, with revised results.

E5.justification: V1 reports prediction uncertainty from 100 stochastic dropout passes, uncertainty distributions, and distribution-based review thresholds; v3 removes this entire annotation-uncertainty reporting component. Separately, annotator comparisons retain means and standard deviations over five random samplings. There is no documented increase in replicates or addition of benchmark confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Benchmark and annotation results are extensively replaced. For example, PG-FDD's AUC is 99.937% in v1 Table 5 and 99.172% in v3 Table 4, under different data and training conditions, so this is not a same-setting decline. V3 adds CCv2, ratio-study, demographic-subgroup, and CLIP+MLP results; the latter reports 99.973% AUC. V1's detailed source-level tables and several annotation-validation results are removed.

T1.justification: Formal revisions concern mathematical definitions rather than new theoretical guarantees. V3 defines vector-scaling and Sinkhorn losses and changes the individual-fairness expression from indicator-style notation to an explicit positive-part penalty with an L2 norm. Uncertainty and average-rank definitions are removed. The SAM derivation remains, and neither version presents substantial theorem/proof development.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a first million-scale demographically annotated AI-face dataset and comprehensive fairness benchmark. The annotation contribution changes from uncertainty-scored, human-corrected labels to a measurement method and learned annotators. The introduction also sharpens the claimed benchmark gap around fairness reliability under changing conditions.

C2.justification: V3 adds a substantive rationale for apparent skin tone rather than race, shifts recommendations toward foundation models, and explains subgroup errors through representation imbalance. It adds interpretations of real/fake balancing and acknowledges that distortions can improve measured fairness while harming utility. The limitation changes from chiefly inaccurate age labels to uncertainty about algorithmic demographic labels generally, with human labeling proposed as future work.

D1.justification: V3 adds source-download/access/license documentation, skin-tone implementation settings, new loss hyperparameters, and human-labeling training and adjudication details. Most decisively, v1 Appendix C.4 says annotator code is available, whereas v3 Appendix E.4 says it will not be released. Dataset-release wording also changes from already released to release following acceptance, despite the retained abstract availability statement.

R1.justification: V3 adds CCv1 and DF40 to the related-benchmark comparison and distinguishes basic fairness evaluation from fairness reliability. It substantially expands the supporting literature on demographic categorization, Monk versus Fitzpatrick skin scales, CLIP bias, imbalance handling, and optimal transport. This revises both annotation rationale and novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The dataset narrative is reorganized from two development/annotation phases into collection, annotation generation, statistics, and quality assessment. Benchmark settings and results become separate sections, and the appendices are reorganized into demographic definitions, dataset details, settings, analyses, and a datasheet. Annotation, interpretation, and limitations passages are extensively rewritten, with a new ethics statement.

P2.justification: The main text switches to two columns. V3 introduces a dataset-comparison Figure 1, moves and revises the face montage, redraws the annotation pipeline, and brings redesigned distribution charts into the main text. Subgroup plots change from relative FPR to absolute FPR, and robustness bars become ratio plots. Numerous uncertainty figures and source-level tables are replaced by new demographic and supplementary displays.

improvement.justification: V3 clarifies demographic definitions and adds useful ratio, age-subgroup, and foundation-model analyses. However, it removes v1's dataset-wide human audit and uncertainty-guided correction, provides no quantitative human validation of the new skin-tone labels, and states that annotator code will be withheld. Table D.9 also reverses gender and skin-tone headings relative to Table 4. These gains and losses affect the benchmark's central annotation credibility and reproducibility, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
